verdict_template.unassured: Nothing is failing; monitoring is still landing on {unassured} of {total} areas, and the plans are filed.
verdict_template.ok: Nothing is blocked and the evidence behind these numbers is fresh.

goals.statement: Every recorded session says who played it and whether they had been coached.
goals.statement_short: recorded sessions do not say who played them or whether they were coached
goals.why_it_matters: The onboarding rebuild's sleeping-spot result was voided because the player had been shown the cot in an earlier session. That fact lives only in prose, so no score I report can be trusted on its own.

measure.label: sessions with recorded conditions, over sessions with a trace

path_to_green.narrative: Backfill the existing folders from the roadmap's own prose, each marked as your word after the fact rather than a measurement, and teach the session puller to write it from now on.

goals.statement: Every blocked project says what would unblock it.
goals.statement_short: a blocked project records no way out
goals.why_it_matters: A blocker with no unblock action never reaches your queue. It goes quiet instead of getting solved.

measure.label: blocked projects with no unblock action
measure.unit: blocked project with no way out

path_to_green.narrative: Write the one sentence that would get each stuck project moving again.

goals.statement: The onboarding rebuild counts as finished: one uncoached first-time player cleared every bar set for it.
goals.statement_short: the onboarding rebuild still has one bar no uncoached first-time player has cleared

path_to_green.narrative: The cot presentation shipped. One uncoached first-time sitting scores the one open bar, the cot being found and used without prompting; the other four bars were met in the last session and do not need re-running.

goals.statement: The build those playtest numbers were measured on is close to what you would ship today.
goals.statement_short: the newest scored session ran on a build far behind what you would ship today
goals.why_it_matters: Evidence rots. Every commit since the session was recorded is a change the score never saw.

path_to_green.narrative: The same fresh sitting re-scores everything on a current build.

goals.statement: Somebody has played the game recently enough for these numbers to mean anything.
goals.statement_short: nobody has played the game in over a week

goals.statement: Taps that achieve nothing stay at or under the bar the last milestone set.
goals.statement_short: taps that achieve nothing are back above the bar the last milestone set
goals.why_it_matters: A tap that does nothing is the game failing to answer. It is the closest thing this project has to a frustration meter.

path_to_green.narrative: Open the newest session in the scrubber and look at what refused.

goals.statement: Nothing has been stuck waiting for longer than a week.
goals.statement_short: something has been stuck waiting for over a week

path_to_green.narrative: The look session and the audio discussion are both waiting on a date from you.

ceo_blocker.consequence: The look guide stays unsigned and the audio direction stays unstarted.

goals.statement: Project plans and program report always up to date
goals.statement_short: CEO asks question about an item on the program report, and we realize the item is not up to date.
goals.why_it_matters: I need absolute trust in the progress we're making, as reported on the program report. If I can't trust the data, then I can use the program report. If I can't use the program report, then what do I use to know the current state of the company? And similarly, how will the entire org have a single source of truth for business-critical data and knowledge?
